name: Bianca Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We're independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we don't sell or campaign. Your answers are confidential, including the parts you wouldn't say at work. What is a normal day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead three complaint agents at a large mobile-network company. We ring people after a tower fault is marked fixed, because the map can be green while a basement flat still has no signal. I was promoted from the phone desk this year and am still learning the network reports; my bachelor's degree is not a radio qualification. I have never used an AI tool, and I keep a callback ledger beside the screen.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58 and live with Joel, who repairs shoes for paying customers. Our daughter and son are grown and live in their own homes. We rent, my manager pay is typical, and we have three months of expenses saved; there are some comparable offices nearby. The landlord will tell us the new rent soon, and we have not checked what pension income we could draw or when.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI stays a small helper, customers will still call when a tower outage is marked fixed but their phone has no signal. I can manage the callback list with my three agents. We have three months of expenses in cash, though the landlord will set a new rent soon and I don't know the number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my agents to phone the callers we marked resolved last night, not just close the complaint. I'd tell the network crew the outage map needs to match what people can do in their own kitchens. I have never used AI and wouldn't call a fresh screen a repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I was promoted from the phone desk this year and am still learning how to read the network reports. My manager pay is typical, Joel's shoe-repair work brings in money when customers come, and there are a few comparable offices nearby. The rent renewal is on my mind even if the technology stays ordinary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I'll have the three agents call back the fourteen households whose signal complaints were closed after the west tower reset. I'll keep the callback ledger in the first plateau year and ask the landlord for written rent-renewal terms before we agree to another year. I'll save 70 monthly only after rent, food and medicine are paid from my wage and Joel's actual repair receipts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy rather than frightened. The job looks steady, but I want the rent amount on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the reset miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The engineer marked the tower green, but the basement flats still had no signal. One older resident went upstairs to make a medical call. A green tower map does not make a basement phone ring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your grown children help with rent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter and son live on their own. They visit on Sundays, but I have not asked them for rent money. Joel and I need to know the new rent before we ask anyone for advice.

say: I'd tell agents to **call households back** before closing tower complaints.
I'd tell the network crew a **green map** can miss a basement.
think: I am **still learning network reports** after promotion from the phone desk.
The unknown rent renewal keeps **our household** on my mind.
do: Keep the **callback ledger** and request written rent renewal before agreeing another year.
Save **70 monthly** only after rent, food and medicine are paid from actual household income.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about rent while work looks steady.
S0.quote: A green tower map does not make a basement phone ring.
fieldNote: The west-tower reset missed **basement flats** despite a green status.
Her worry is the **pending rent**, not immediate job loss.
New saving depends on **paid wages and receipts** covering essentials.

steps.text: Call fourteen west-tower households to verify signal tomorrow
Request written rent renewal before agreeing to another year
Save 70 monthly only after rent, food and medicine are paid from actual income

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing replies, checking outage reports, planning callbacks and answering customers fill my team's day. A stronger system could do those tasks and leave one person for the hardest complaints. The engineer still climbs a tower for now, but my job is a phone and a report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for a test on last month's false 'resolved' cases before anyone shortens phone hours. I'd tell callers they need a person to hear that the signal is still down. I'd ask the company for the proposed staffing rota in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could lose this junior manager post if the company combines several complaint desks. I know how to calm a caller, but I have never used AI and I am still learning the reporting side. Three months cash would help with a search, though Joel's repair income alone wouldn't cover rent and medicine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January I'd ask for a paid old-case test, with the network analyst checking the tower logs and the director approving the trial. I'd keep the callback ledger until the results and staffing decision are written down. I'd apply for posted local service-manager roles after checking duties, pay and bus hours, staying here until a signed offer with Joel's confirmed repair income covers rent, food and medicine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own post. A test can be fair and still show the company it wants fewer people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the new complaint screen?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a trained analyst offers paid instruction, the director approves it and I can see the original caller record beside the model's answer. I would not learn on a live medical call. Until then I can still check whether a promised callback happened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the old-case test useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The basement complaint that the reset closed too early. If the system marks it resolved again, I want the analyst to show which log line fooled it. A closed complaint is not a working phone.

say: I'd ask for **old false-closure testing** before phone hours shrink.
I'd demand a **human caller route** for unresolved outages.
think: My **junior manager post** could disappear in a desk merger.
Joel's repair income cannot cover **rent and medicine** without my wage.
do: Request a **paid old-case test** only with analyst checks and director approval.
Keep the **callback ledger** while trial results and staffing decision are pending.
Apply for **posted local service roles** after duty, pay and bus checks; leave after affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my own post despite a search cushion.
S1.quote: A closed complaint is not a working phone.
fieldNote: She wants the false tower closure in a **paid approved test**.
She may accept instruction later but does **not yet use AI**.
Another role needs **viable duties** and workable pay and bus travel before applying.

steps.text: Request paid false-closure test only with network analyst checks and director approval
Keep callback ledger while old-case results and staffing decision are pending
Apply for service roles after duty, pay and bus checks; leave only for affordable signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 full AGI could read the tower logs, answer calls and decide which outage gets a crew faster than my desk. I expect our complaint manager role to go, and similar desks nearby could go too. Joel's hands still repair shoes until capable robots arrive around 2031, while his bookings and prices are thinking tasks that change in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my agents to ask for notice terms in writing. I'd tell Joel we should cancel the deposit for the planned rail holiday before it is due. I'd tell callers to keep a record of failed calls so they can challenge an automatic closure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my manager wage to end, and Joel's variable repair money plus three months cash may not cover the new rent for long. I'd be awake calculating what happens if the landlord raises it just when the desk closes. I cannot retire simply because I am sixty; I do not know the pension date or amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd ask human resources for written notice and severance figures, cancel the rail-holiday deposit before payment and request the landlord's written rent renewal. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my wage ends, I'd apply for posted local paid work after checking duties and bus travel, accepting only a signed offer whose wage with Joel's confirmed receipts covers rent, food and medicine. I'd check public-help eligibility and apply only if we qualify; I would speak to the landlord before rent is late if combined income falls short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. The rent letter and a lost wage could arrive in the same week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you work on tower repairs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never climbed a tower, and I don't have the safety training. The crew's lifting stays physical until robots around 2031, but its planning and diagnosis face AGI in 2028. I would not put my name on a climbing application without a real paid place and a health check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They would both still be adults. I would tell them a holiday is postponed and that we are checking real wages; I would not ask them to solve our rent. If we needed a one-off stay, Joel and I would ask whether either could offer it and respect a no.

say: I'd ask for **written notice terms** for the agents.
I'd tell callers to keep **failed-call records** for disputes.
think: I expect my **manager wage to end** by 2028.
Joel's repairs and three months cash may not cover **higher rent** through a search.
do: Request **written terms** for notice and rent; check public-help eligibility before applying.
Cancel the **rail-holiday deposit** before paying it.
Apply for **posted local work** after duty and bus checks; accept only signed offer whose pay with Joel's confirmed receipts covers essentials.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by a likely lost wage and uncertain rent.
S2.quote: The rent letter and a lost wage could arrive in the same week.
fieldNote: She does not claim **tower-climbing skill** as an AGI refuge.
Physical crew tasks face **2031 robots**; complaint thinking work faces AGI in 2028.
Public help requires **eligibility**, and family shelter would require an offer.

steps.text: Request written notice, severance and rent renewal terms now
Apply for local work after duty and bus checks; accept only affordable signed offer
Check public-help eligibility and apply only if household qualifies

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me see the rent renewals and pension statement before my desk faces AGI in 2031. Network crews still climb until capable robots arrive around 2034, but the complaint answers and schedules change in 2031. I don't see a safe desk just by moving to another phone company.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the company for a date on the complaint desk changes. I'd tell Joel we should put the pension amount beside the rent number every year. I'd tell callers to keep their own record of a failed signal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may earn this wage until 2031, and three months cash gives us some time to compare offers. I don't know whether a pension would let me stop at sixty-three, and Joel's repair bookings vary. Another local service job could pay us, but its calls face AGI too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I'd request my written pension eligibility date and monthly estimate and compare it with rent, food and medicine. I'd save 85 monthly only after my wage and Joel's actual repair receipts pay those bills, aiming for five months cash if work holds. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd apply for posted local paid roles only if their wage with Joel's confirmed receipts covers essentials; I'd leave this job only for a signed offer or actual pension income that truly pays our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my pay, though the years allow a real comparison. A guessed pension is not a deposit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you rely on Joel's shop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Shoe repairs pay by completed job, not by my calendar. If bookings fall, the 85 transfer stops. I would not count a customer who only asked for a price as paid income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change houses?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not before the landlord gives us a rent number. We could compare smaller rentals if the new rent is too high, but I would only move if Joel agrees and the total rent, deposit and travel cost are actually affordable. A cheaper listing is not a signed lease.

say: I'd ask for a **complaint-desk date** from the company.
I'd tell Joel to compare **pension and rent** yearly.
think: I may earn until 2031, but **pension eligibility** is unknown.
Joel's variable bookings make **actual receipts** important for cash planning.
do: Request **pension eligibility** and monthly amount in 2027.
Save **85 monthly** only after my wage and Joel's paid repairs cover essentials, stopping if his bookings fall.
Apply for **posted local work** after 2031 only with affordable confirmed pay; leave after signed offer or adequate pension.
feel: I feel **anxious** about later pay while able to compare options.
S3.quote: A cheaper listing is not a signed lease.
fieldNote: She would compare rentals if rent rises; moving needs **Joel's agreement** and real costs.
She counts completed repairs, not **unpaid enquiries**, in household income.
She does not assume **pension access** at sixty-three.

steps.text: Request written pension eligibility date and monthly estimate in 2027
Save 85 monthly only after wage and paid repairs cover bills; stop if Joel's bookings fall
Apply for local work with affordable pay; leave only after signed offer or sufficient pension

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be sixty-eight in 2036. Our grown children will have their own bills, and I don't know our rent or pension amount then. Complaint decisions face AGI in 2036, and capable robots may do physical tower work and shoe repairs around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the company to publish desk-change dates. I'd tell Joel we should keep the rent and pension figures in one folder. I'd tell our children we are planning, not sending them a bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade might let us reach a larger cushion if both incomes hold, but the rent can change before 2036. I would not call sixty-eight a retirement plan unless actual pension income plus Joel's confirmed repair pay covers rent, food and medicine. My manager desk could still vanish even if I keep every callback ledger clean.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'd request written pension eligibility and estimated monthly pay and get the landlord's rent renewal in writing. I'd save 110 monthly only after rent, food and medicine are paid from confirmed wages and completed repair receipts, pausing if Joel's bookings fall. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if pension plus Joel's confirmed pay does not cover essentials, I'd apply for posted local work with a wage and bus route I can manage; I'd consider a smaller rental only after Joel agrees and actual rent, deposit and travel costs are affordable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a new rent alongside a vanishing desk, though a decade gives me time to gather facts. I will not set a retirement date from a birthday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave town to find work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would first check the posted roles we can reach by bus. Our daughter lives farther away, but she has not offered us a room or a job. A move needs a real lease, Joel's agreement and a wage or pension that pays for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pension is enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I could stop paid work if eligibility is real and Joel and I agree on the budget. I would not take a job only to say I have one. We would keep cash for rent changes, because a pension figure can stay still while rent rises.

The complaint desk can vanish even with **careful records**.
do: Request **pension and rent terms** in writing this winter.
Save **110 monthly** only after essentials from confirmed paid income; pause if Joel's bookings fall.
Apply for **bus-accessible work** if pension plus Joel's confirmed pay falls short; consider smaller rental only with his agreement and affordable costs.
feel: I feel **anxious** about rent and the desk despite time to prepare.
S4.quote: I will not set a retirement date from a birthday.
fieldNote: She ties retirement to **actual eligibility** and household income, not age alone.
A smaller rental needs **Joel's agreement** and real rent, deposit and travel costs.
Savings pause if **paid shoe-repair bookings** fall.

steps.text: Request pension eligibility, monthly amount and written rent renewal this winter

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I expect my complaint manager wage to end while the rent may rise and Joel's repair income varies. Written notice, a real paid local opening, verified help eligibility and a pension statement with an actual date would help. Three months cash buys a short search, not a comfortable retirement.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the resident who climbed the stairs to make a medical call whether the green outage map helped. A signal bar is not a voice at the other end. I want someone to check the basement before closing the complaint.
